processing.normal: Built-in generation followed by fixed 1024/1254 isotropic premultiplied BICUBIC normalization. Only detached exterior components with alpha <= 2 were removed; no part repainting or per-frame fitting.
processing.pixel: Only the accepted same-phase normal was supplied to built-in generation. Fixed 128/1254 nearest sampling, alpha >= 128 binarization and nearest shared 32-color mapping without dithering. Uniform whole-frame Y shifts: 01 -3, 02 -3, 03 -2, 04 -3 pixels; zero clipping and exact inverse RGBA checks.

paletteReference.use: Finishing palette only; not a generation reference and not reused as an animation frame.

residualCaveats: Phase01 planned foot lift 20 normal pixels was exceeded by the actual 39. Phase03 targeted the achieved opposite amplitude 39 and reached 42. Planned values have not been retrospectively changed.
Passing body-rise target was 4 normal pixels. Phase02 head top rose 16 and central protrusion 10; phase04 head top rose 18 and central protrusion 17. These are not exact rigid 4-pixel translations.
Pixel03 support-to-swing sole separation is 8 pixels versus 5 in the same-normal 128 diagnostic, a 3-pixel swing amplification rather than assumed quantization.

From phase03 to phase04, the pixel right-foot bottom moves down 1 pixel (108 to 109), while the normal diagnostic moves up 1 (110 to 109). The foot moves inward and remains lifted, but its vertical path is not identical.
Small pixel silhouette and registration differences remain. Phase04 support is 1 pixel lower than its normal diagnostic, while the passing foot and central protrusion bottom agree.
Face color areas, small tooth, eye reflections, shading, neck and stripe simplification, and foot contours vary among pixel frames.
The small central underside protrusion has unidentified anatomy. Its shape and torso-relative placement are retained; it is not declared an additional supporting leg.
Root depth, exact forward stride, world displacement and collision synchronization are not established by this S-view sequence.
